fichas.title: Asymmetrical two-span beam structural system
fichas.summary: The floor spans across the building, with supporting beams running along it. A central support beam and columns beside the corridor are separate from the corridor wall. The arrangement allows flexible, reversible layouts, maintains clear passage between column and wall, and is suitable where there is no suspended ceiling or for enclosed car parking with an access route along the building.

fichas.title: Multi-span beam structural system
fichas.summary: The floor spans along the building, with supporting beams running across it from an external column through a centre column to an external column. The system permits flexible, reversible layouts. Additional sound-insulation measures are required because of the insufficient floor density. It is described as suitable for enclosed car parking with an access route along the building.

fichas.title: Three-span beam structural system
fichas.summary: The floor spans across the building, with supporting beams running along the building on both sides of the corridor in the middle span. The corridor wall may be load-bearing or bracing to increase longitudinal rigidity. A masonry corridor wall cannot be altered, limiting flexibility in room depth. This system is not suitable above enclosed car parking; a load-bearing corridor wall is described as cost-effective, especially with greater building depth and longer column spacing.

fichas.title: Slab acting as beam structural system
fichas.summary: Supporting beams span freely across the building from external column to external column. The system permits flexible, reversible planning but requires a suspended ceiling and is described as uneconomical overall, suitable only for column-free superstructures. Services run across the building between webs; longitudinal runs through beam cutouts are impractical. The reduced supporting-beam height is associated with vibration and high deflection.

fichas.title: Construction and structural planning for office buildings
fichas.summary: The page compares construction choices and structural systems for two-row office buildings. It discusses loading assumptions, ceiling heights, slab options, services routing, façade and column planning, cantilevers, bracing, and solid versus lightweight partitions. Solid partitions can replace columns and supporting beams or provide rigidity, but are not reversible. Lightweight partitions can potentially be relocated, though they may delay room-layout decisions.
